info.title: OpenAsy Access API
info.summary: SSH access to servers only when someone asked and someone else approved, with certificates that expire with it.
info.description:
Every screen of Access uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Asking for access, approving it and getting a certificate are a person's acts: they need the session of someone signed in with a second factor or through an identity provider, never an API token. Everything else takes a session or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003). The CA's public key and the revocation list need no sign-in, for the servers.

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

get.description: Needs the viewer role. From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.
Needs the viewer role. What waits for approval, what is open now, and how long people wait.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

get.description: Not a secret, so no sign-in is needed: provisioning scripts fetch it for TrustedUserCAKeys.

An OpenSSH key revocation list (KRL) naming the certificates of grants that ended early, until they would have expired. Servers fetch it every minute for RevokedKeys; it holds serials only, so no sign-in is needed.

post.description: Needs the admin role. With its policy: the logins one may ask for, the longest grant and the approvals needed.

put.description: Needs the admin role. A server with open grants cannot be renamed: its name is in their certificates.

delete.description: Needs the admin role. Not while requests wait or grants are open for it. Its requests stay in the record.

get.summary: Shell commands that make a server trust Access
get.description: Needs the viewer role. Run once as root on the server: it trusts the CA for the server's own logins only, with a principals file per login, and fetches the revocation list every minute.
Needs the viewer role. Newest first, at most 200.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: true for the signed-in person's own.

post.description: Needs the viewer role. For yourself: a person signed in with a second factor, or through an identity provider. API tokens cannot. One request per server and login may wait or be open at a time.

get.summary: A request, its certificates and its record

post.description: Needs the editor role. By a person other than the requester, with a second factor: a try at one's own is refused and recorded. The grant starts with the last approval the server needs and lasts as long as asked for.
Needs the editor role. By a person other than the requester, with a second factor.
Needs the viewer role. While it waits.
Needs the viewer role. The requester ends their own; an editor revokes anyone's. Its certificates go on the revocation list. Sessions open on the server are not closed.

post.summary: Get a certificate for your public key
post.description: Needs the viewer role. Only the requester, with a second factor, while the grant is open. The certificate is valid on the grant's server only, for its login, until the grant ends. Your private key never leaves your computer.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Every request, approval, grant, certificate, change to servers, sign-in and refused attempt, newest first. Rows are never changed or removed.

get.summary: The whole audit log as CSV
get.description: Needs the viewer role. Oldest first. Cells that a spreadsheet would run as a formula start with an apostrophe.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Access runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Access origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_access_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003). It cannot ask for, approve or use access.

adminToken.description: Only when Access is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

publicKey.description: One line for sshd's TrustedUserCAKeys file.

Ca.description: The Ed25519 certificate authority that signs every certificate. Its private key never leaves Access, sealed with the install's key.

name.description: A host name; it is part of every principal, login@name.

address.description: Host name or IP address people connect to.

logins.description: The Unix accounts on the server one may ask to log in as.

maxMinutes.description: The longest grant one may ask for.

approvals.description: How many people other than the requester must approve.

principal.description: What its certificates carry, and the server's principals file lists: login@server.

status.description: active is an open grant; ended ran out or was ended by the requester; revoked was ended by someone else.

fingerprint.description: Of the person's own public key.

revoked.description: Its grant ended early: it is on the revocation list until it would have expired.

ticket.description: An incident or change, such as INC-2291.

publicKey.description: One line of your ~/.ssh/id_*.pub: Ed25519, ECDSA, RSA of 2048 bits or more, or a security key.

certificate.description: Save it next to your key as id_ed25519-cert.pub (or the name of your key with -cert.pub); ssh uses it on its own.

command.description: How to connect, such as ssh deploy@10.0.0.5.

action.description: Such as request.create, request.approve, grant.start, grant.end, grant.revoke, certificate.issue, server.update or auth.sign-in.

result.description: denied for an attempt that was refused, such as approving one's own request.

next.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last.

medianWaitMinutes.description: From request to grant, over the last 30 days.
